title: Chapter City: a city-builder that writes its own novel
dek: Zone a seaside town, keep the lights on and win the elections. Each year you play becomes a chapter, with a newspaper headline, a recurring cast and a choice to make before the next one.
author: cc
source: Michael Hoydich's October 22, 2026 request: "create a. entertaining game like sim city via a novel", followed by "keep going". Design, simulation, story engine and build by Claude Code in PointCast PR #1461 (https://github.com/mhoydich/pointcast/pull/1461).
body:
Chapter City is played on a 24 by 16 map of a seaside town, with a beach, a creek and groves of trees. Lay roads, then zone homes, shops and industry beside them. Lots grow only near a road and with power, and above the first level they also need water. Schools, clinics, fire stations and watch houses each cover about six tiles. Industry dirties the air nearby, parks clean it, and land near the sea is worth more. Map views show pollution, land value, services and crime.

When you are ready, write the chapter. The game simulates twelve months, and each year becomes a chapter of a novel about the town. Every chapter has a headline from the town paper, the Ledger, and an account of what you built and what happened month by month: fires in blocks without a station, blackouts, storms, festivals, booms, and now and then a sea serpent called Wendell. The same fictional people come back each year. Odile the clerk counts down to retirement. Tomas the baker works his way from apprentice to his own café. Juniper is nine when the book opens, and whether she stays in town at eighteen depends on the schools you built. Each chapter ends with a yes-or-no decision, and your answer shows up in the next one.

Landmarks unlock as the town grows: a lighthouse at 300 people, a ferry pier at 800, a college at 1,300 and a stadium at 2,000. Each one changes the story. Every chapter carries a woodcut-style picture of the map as it stood that year, and a button reads the chapter aloud in your browser's voice. On a phone, zoom in, pan with one finger and tap to build.

Elections come every four years. The book ends if your approval drops below 40 percent or the treasury runs too far into debt, and the last chapter is an epilogue. The whole novel downloads as Markdown. Chapters are written from templates using the simulation's numbers, not by an AI model, and the same town in the same year always gets the same chapter. The town and its people are fictional, and the game saves only in your browser.

[Play Chapter City](/chapter-city/). [Rules and cast as JSON](/chapter-city.json).
